messages.text: Happy to help. What's going on with it, or are you looking to pick one out?
When my miner is connected to my Wi-Fi, it creates his own IP address.I'm having a hard time getting into the I.P address for monitoring

Quickest way in: open your router's admin page and look at the connected devices / DHCP client list. The miner shows up there with its IP, type that into a browser on the same network. The unit's own display usually shows the IP too.

Which model is it, and does it have a screen?

For hands-on help fast, our Discord is the best spot: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , post there and mention @nullhashrate (JD).

That one's not a unit I've got specs for on my side, so I don't want to guess at its interface.

General thing worth trying: if it's still broadcasting its own hotspot, it hasn't joined your Wi-Fi properly. Connect to that hotspot, open 192.168.4.1, re-enter your Wi-Fi details, then find it in your router's device list.

I've asked JD, who handles the hardware, to pick this up. Fastest route is Discord right now: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.
Handed to the team · Model not in our product facts, cannot confirm its interface or default IP

JD's been pinged and can jump in here, so stay in the chat if you can. If you step away, you'll get the answer by email.

In the meantime, does the miner still show its own Wi-Fi network in your phone's list?
No it's now connected to my wifi

Good, that's the hard part done. So it has an IP from your router now.

Log into your router (usually 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1) and open the connected devices list. The miner will be there, often named something like bitaxe or axe. Take that IP, type it straight into a browser on the same network, no https, just the number.

If the page won't load, tell me what the browser says and whether your phone is on the same Wi-Fi band.
No it dose not work can't load

Most likely cause: your phone or laptop is on a different network from the miner, a guest network or AP isolation on the router blocks them seeing each other. Put your device on the same main 2.4GHz network and try again.

Did you find the miner's IP in the router list, and what number was it?

Then your router's on 10.0.0.x, so try typing it exactly as http://10.0.0.43 in the address bar. Phones often turn a bare number into a search instead of loading it.

If that still fails, power cycle the miner, wait two minutes, and check the router list again, the IP can change.

Is your phone on 10.0.0.x too? You can see that in your Wi-Fi settings under IP address.

Same subnet, so the next suspect is client isolation on the router, it's often on by default and stops devices talking to each other. Look for "AP isolation" or "client isolation" in the Wi-Fi settings and turn it off.

Worth trying from a laptop too, and a different browser.

If neither works, JD is the one to take it from here, and he's quickest on Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , post and mention @nullhashrate. He's also picking this chat up.

Log into your router the same way you found the IP list, usually 10.0.0.1 in a browser, then go to the Wi-Fi or Wireless settings. The setting sits under advanced wireless options, named AP isolation, client isolation or guest mode. Untick it and save, the router reboots for a minute.

Which router do you have, brand and model? I'll tell you exactly where it lives in that menu.

On Xfinity it's in the xFi app, not the router page. Open the app, go to the miner under connected devices, and check it isn't on the guest network. Then More, My Services, Advanced Security, and turn it off temporarily. xFi Advanced Security is the usual thing blocking local access to a miner.

Try 10.0.0.43 again right after. Did that change anything?
